subtitle: Lesson 15 · Security Operations on the Platform

eyebrow: Not an Incident with a scarier name
code:
Regular Incident:                 Security Incident:
"what's broken, how fast           "have we been compromised,
 can we restore service?"           who did it, what's now required?"
caption: Same mechanics, a fundamentally different kind of problem.

eyebrow: Built on task, with its own workflow
code:
Regular Incident lifecycle:          Security Incident lifecycle:
New -> In Progress -> Resolved       Analysis -> Contain -> Eradicate
  -> Closed                            -> Recover -> Review -> Closed
caption: sn_si_incident extends task, the same pattern you already know.

eyebrow: Three phases, in order, on purpose

steps.label: Containment
steps.sub: stop it spreading, before you fully understand it

steps.label: Eradication
steps.sub: remove the actual root cause, not just the symptom

steps.label: Recovery
steps.sub: restore operation only once the threat is truly gone

code:
Recovery before Eradication finishes:
  reconnects a STILL-INFECTED system
  to the network — the mistake this
  phase order exists to prevent
caption: Skipping ahead undoes containment.

steps.label: Evidence, not notes
steps.sub: work notes may be read by counsel or a regulator

steps.label: Notification duties
steps.sub: a breach can trigger obligations an outage never has

steps.label: Post-incident review
steps.sub: the record isn't finished until the org has learned from it

subtitle: From responding to incidents, to preventing the next one.
